chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one with a broken bone and the one with stomach illness, the Jamarah is pelted on their behalf. He (peace be upon him) said: And the children, the Jamarah is pelted on their behalf.

key_terms.الْكَسِيرُ: The one with a broken bone
key_terms.يُرْمَى: Is pelted (referring to throwing stones at the Jamarah)

ai.seo_question: Who can have the Jamarah pelting performed on their behalf during Haj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of delegating the Jamarah ritual to a representative for those unable to perform it due to illness or age, specifically citing 'al-kasir' (broken bone) and 'al-mabtoon' (stomach ailment) as examples of valid impediments. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that physical incapacity or youth exempts the individual from the personal obligation, allowing a proxy to fulfill the rite on their behalf. This ruling highlights the flexibility within Hajj jurisprudence to accommodate the sick and children, ensuring the ritual's completion without undue hardship.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, and Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The disabled, and the one with stomach illness, (the Jamarah) would be pelted on both their behalf’. Heasws said: ‘And the children, (the Jamarah) would be pelted on their behalf’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar and ‘ Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is permissible to throw pebbles on behalf of one who has a broken part or has stomach illness and so also is the rule about children.’”
